Apple (AAPL) Shares Bought by Cedar Capital LLC Posted by Dante Gardener | Jun 13th, 2018
Cedar Capital LLC increased its holdings in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 37.1% during the 4th quarter, according to the company in its most recent 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The firm owned 5,374 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after buying an additional 1,455 shares during the quarter. Cedar Capital LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $909,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Other large investors have also modified their holdings of the company. Accredited Investors Inc. boosted its position in Apple by 26.2% in the 3rd quarter. Accredited Investors Inc. now owns 35,970 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,544,000 after purchasing an additional 7,461 shares in the last quarter. Zevin Asset Management LLC boosted its position in Apple by 3.9% in the 3rd quarter. Zevin Asset Management LLC now owns 38,216 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,890,000 after purchasing an additional 1,434 shares in the last quarter. Investment Partners Ltd. OH ADV boosted its position in Apple by 8.6% in the 3rd quarter. Investment Partners Ltd. OH ADV now owns 5,199 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $801,000 after purchasing an additional 411 shares in the last quarter. Brightworth boosted its position in Apple by 1,768.6% in the 3rd quarter. Brightworth now owns 66,636 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $10,270,000 after purchasing an additional 63,070 shares in the last quarter. Finally, NewFocus Financial Group LLC boosted its position in Apple by 0.7% in the 3rd quarter. NewFocus Financial Group LLC now owns 80,882 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $12,465,000 after purchasing an additional 532 shares in the last quarter. Institutional investors own 58.13% of the company’s stock. Get Apple alerts:
Several research firms have commented on AAPL. BidaskClub lowered Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating in a research report on Friday, June 8th. UBS Group set a $210.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Wednesday. Atlantic Securities restated a “neutral” rating and issued a $185.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Wednesday, May 2nd. Zacks Investment Research upgraded Apple from a “sell” rating to a “hold” rating in a research report on Thursday, May 3rd. Finally, BMO Capital Markets increased their target price on Apple from $166.00 to $171.00 and gave the company a “market perform” rating in a research report on Wednesday, May 2nd. One analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have given a hold rating, thirty-one have assigned a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company. The stock has an average rating of “Buy” and an average price target of $205.87.
Apple stock traded down $1.58 during midday trading on Wednesday, reaching $190.70. 21,479,713 shares of the stock traded hands, compared to its average volume of 19,976,752. Apple has a 12-month low of $142.20 and a 12-month high of $194.20. The stock has a market capitalization of $970.30 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 20.71, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.57 and a beta of 1.29. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a current ratio of 1.46 and a quick ratio of 1.37.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. The business had revenue of $61.14 billion during the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $60.94 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The business’s quarterly revenue was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same quarter last year, the business posted $2.10 EPS. equities research analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.42 earnings per share for the current year.
The company also recently declared a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Shareholders of record on Monday, May 14th were given a dividend of $0.73 per share. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. The ex-dividend date was Friday, May 11th. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.53%. Apple’s payout ratio is 31.70%.
Apple declared that its board has initiated a share buyback plan on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This repurchase authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to reacquire up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares repurchase plans are typically an indication that the company’s management believes its stock is undervalued.
In other news, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Tuesday, April 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The transaction was disclosed in a document filed with the SEC, which is accessible through this hyperlink . Also, COO Jeffrey E. Williams sold 15,653 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, June 8th. The shares were sold at an average price of $190.94, for a total value of $2,988,783.82. Following the completion of the transaction, the chief operating officer now directly owns 147,819 shares in the company, valued at approximately $28,224,559.86. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . In the last ninety days, insiders have sold 272,506 shares of company stock worth $48,367,350. 0.06% of the stock is currently owned by corporate insiders.
Apple Profile
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. The company also sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.
